solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wallachian ruler restructured DVLA

indicators.note: something restructured has had its parts rebuilt in a different arrangement

blocks.note: the UK driving licence agency's initials, taken as written

explanation.surface: A medieval prince is pictured as having overhauled Britain's vehicle licensing office.
explanation.walkthrough: The DVLA is the British agency that issues driving licences; its four letters rearrange into the ruler's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlad the Impaler was the fifteenth-century prince of Wallachia, the historical inspiration for Dracula.

clue.text: Reveal criminal drinking hotel port

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are bent out of order
one who drinks takes something inside, so one set of letters swallows another

blocks.note: taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone urges exposing a crook caught drinking at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reveal' reads as the definition at the front, but it is fodder; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French seaport on the Channel at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Peg to prosper endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to prosper is to do well

explanation.surface: An odd motto urging a peg to keep thriving for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrase is run together and loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a round wooden pin used in joinery to hold two pieces together, which is a kind of peg.

clue.text: Rascal in Virginia and Georgia with 007

blocks.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia
007 is James Bond's code number

explanation.surface: A villain loose in two southern US states, teamed up with James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: The state abbreviations are the US postal codes; 'in' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond can be a rogue or scoundrel as well as a wanderer, so it works as another word for a rascal.

clue.text: Struggle avoided periodically

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A conflict that was dodged now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete or contend with others, so as a verb it means to strive or struggle against a rival.

clue.text: Drink playing a part in bootlegging era legitimised

indicators.note: something that plays a part in a whole is only a portion of it, so the letters sit inside the words

blocks.note: runs across the ends and start of these three words

explanation.surface: A beverage that featured in the Prohibition years of bootleg liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans bootlegGING ERA LEgitimised; ginger ale was in fact popular as a mixer for bootleg spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a carbonated soft beverage flavoured with ginger, often used as a mixer.

clue.text: Pub profit to negotiate

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
profit is gain

explanation.surface: Haggling over the takings of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A straight two-part build; the infinitive 'to negotiate' matches the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over terms or price, discussing a deal until both sides agree.

clue.text: Steals nothing reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how a word is said

blocks.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A news line insisting that nothing at all is being stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: Nix, slang for nothing, is said the same as the British slang word for steals.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick something is to steal it, so nicks means pinches or pilfers.

clue.text: Say farewell: head for Chinese meal

indicators.note: to say a word is to speak it, so its pronunciation counts rather than spelling

blocks.note: ciao is an Italian goodbye
main means chief or head

explanation.surface: An instruction to say goodbye and head off for a Chinese dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like part of 'say farewell' but signals that both pieces are spoken: ciao and main give the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of stir-fried noodles with vegetables and meat, a staple of takeaways.

clue.text: Grain cost reduced by penny

indicators.note: to reduce something by an amount is to take that amount away from it

blocks.note: the cost is the price
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: The cost of grain has dropped by a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the P from the front of the word for cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is a cereal crop whose small seeds are a staple food across much of the world.

clue.text: Eggs left somewhat out of round?

blocks.note: ova is Latin for eggs
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Eggs left slightly misshapen, not quite spherical.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a shape a bit out of true from a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an elongated circle, so it describes a round shape that has been squashed or stretched.

clue.text: Crack from cleric and fool in church

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so letters go within others

blocks.note: Rev is the short title of a reverend
an ass is a fool
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wisecrack from a vicar and a clown inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' reads as a joke in the surface; the definition is a split. CE, the Church of England, wraps the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep open fissure in a glacier or ice sheet, a large crack.

clue.text: Chase with army somehow ducking shots?

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some undefined way, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pursuit by soldiers, with the quarry dodging gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface makes 'shots' bullets; here they are photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone camera-shy dislikes being photographed and so avoids having pictures taken.

clue.text: Dotty blamed for disorder

indicators.note: dotty means slightly mad, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slightly mad person gets the blame for causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' reads like a name being blamed; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after an old London asylum, means a scene of uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Bloater’s not a bad seafood option

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out
bad means gone wrong, so the remaining letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: the word with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smoked herring is said to be a decent choice from the fish menu.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloater is a smoked herring, so the surface stays in the seafood world; the 'S works as a letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster is a shellfish served as a restaurant dish, one of the choices on a fish menu.

clue.text: Runs into an elderly poet

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so one letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
elderly means old

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into an aged poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elderly poet' looks like a single definition, but 'elderly' is wordplay and only 'poet' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian English poet and critic, author of Dover Beach.

clue.text: Pride issue about copper in library

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so letters are placed within others

blocks.note: on means about, as in a talk on a topic
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
lib is a short form of library

explanation.surface: A dispute about a policeman in a library over pride, perhaps a magazine edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer but is the metal; a pride is a group of lions and its issue is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a family group of lions, and issue means offspring, so a young lion is a pride's issue.

clue.text: Character suffered in flight

blocks.note: an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery
borne means suffered or endured

explanation.surface: A personality who had a hard time while travelling by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In flight' could mean running away; here it means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne is carried through the air, flying aloft rather than resting on the ground.

clue.text: Rodent entering that is angry

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a rat is a rodent
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A rodent comes in and someone is furious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is the abbreviation for 'that is', but only 'that' is used, leaving 'is' to link; some solvers will read 'that is' together as IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym meaning furious or incensed, describing someone full of rage.

clue.text: Quack keeping two ducks closer?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds others

blocks.note: a quack is a doctor, abbreviated DR
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck's quack and two ducks drawing nearer, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' is a duck's call in the surface but a fake doctor here; 'closer' is not 'nearer' but a thing that closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is what closes an opening such as a room or cupboard, hence playfully a closer.

clue.text: Search for water — amount round wicket

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a dose is an amount of medicine
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: Looking for water, measuring how much lies around a cricket wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: W for wicket is a cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to look for underground water with a divining rod, a practice also called water divining.

clue.text: Large having eaten seconds, restrict diet

indicators.note: what has been eaten is inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: fat means large
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Someone big has gone back for second helpings and needs to cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' suggests extra helpings but is just the unit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food for a period, an extreme way of limiting what one eats.

clue.text: Something from Pret in Kentish Town?

blocks.note: first meaning: an item sold at Pret a Manger
second meaning: a town in the county of Kent

explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a district of London, so the surface suggests a branch there; split it and it means a town in Kent. Pret a Manger is a British chain selling ready-made lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Pret is best known for its packaged bread-based lunches, and the historic Cinque Port in Kent shares the name.

clue.text: Neither number right

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Neither of the figures is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: in 'I can't, nor can she' the word does the job of 'neither'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are negative conjunctions introducing a further denial, as in 'nor did I' versus 'neither did I'.

clue.text: Shopper needs carrier taking drink outside

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece holds another
placed outside means wrapped around, so the second piece encloses the first

blocks.note: a tray carries plates and cups
beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A customer needs a bag to carry a drink out of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to shop someone is to inform on them to the police, so a shopper is an informer, not a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper in this slang sense is a grass or informer, someone who betrays another to the authorities.

clue.text: Italian island having strength for revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns a full circle, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: able means having the strength or capacity

explanation.surface: An Italian island strong enough to stage an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests political rebellion, apt for Napoleon's place of exile, but here it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is a Tuscan island off Italy's west coast, famous as Napoleon's first place of exile.
